title: generate() picks 'first active vendor' as Decades vendor â€” fragile defaulting
detail: Line 384: `const vr = await apiGet(`/${EntitySets.vendors}?$filter=dcfg_active_flag eq true&$select=dcfg_vendorid&$top=1`); vendorId = vr.value?.[0]?.dcfg_vendorid`. Picks whichever active vendor happens to be first in the default sort order. On a fresh tenant with multiple active vendors, the 'first one' could be Acme HVAC instead of Decades Construction Group. The subsequent patch (lines 385-390) then writes the Decades signer info to the wrong vendor record, corrupting its data. The 'Decades vendor' should be identified by a canonical flag or ID pulled from dcfg_configs.
recommendedFix: Add a dcfg_configs entry `dcfg_decades_vendor_id` (the GUID of the canonical Decades vendor). Read via getEnvVar and use as the hardcoded-but-configurable vendor id. Fallback to the current 'first active vendor' only if the config is missing.

title: MSA-rates create loops are sequential â€” one POST per location type
detail: Lines 440-467: both the uniform branch (lines 440-452) and the type-based branch (lines 453-467) use sequential for-loops with await inside. With 6-8 location types, that's 6-8 sequential POSTs per proposal generation. Parallelizing cuts wall-clock generation time by ~4-5 seconds.
recommendedFix: Promise.all both loops. Same pattern as CR-0305, CR-0300. Minor risk of Dataverse rate-limiting at 8 concurrent POSTs, acceptable.
